{{Argument
|summary=Alcohol is one of the few legal drugs because its producers rely on financial lobby groups to persuade legislators, through practices bordering on corruption, to adopt the most lenient possible rules.

|article=Drogues: la prohibition, une efficacité illusoire

}}{{Quote
|quote=Investigators at the University of Connecticut produced a 60,000-page report identifying no fewer than 145 instances of fabricated or falsified data. This investigation completely discredits not only those fraudulent studies but also the others: why manipulate studies if wine's beneficial effects had really been proved? Might some scientists have taken bribes from wine-industry lobbyists? That appears to be the case.

A 60,000-page report is no small matter; one imagines there must have been a great deal to say.

The [http://tempsreel.nouvelobs.com/les-Internets-vous-parlent/20120116.OBS8929/le-vin-bon-pour-la-sante-des-etudes-etaient-bidonnees.html exposure] of this scientific fraud is far from an isolated case. It is much more widespread than we can imagine: scientists are, first and foremost, human beings, and therefore fallible and corruptible. Tell me who funds you, and I will tell you who you are.

|date=13 June 2013
